---
title: SkyPilot
---

[SkyPilot](https://docs.skypilot.ai/) provisions compute and launches workloads across clouds, Kubernetes, Slurm, and SSH node pools. It is an external developer tool rather than part of the `qrt` Python package. The tutorials exist as a point of reference for QRT users who want to run workloads on on-prem or cloud infrastructure.

Keep the boundary simple:

- QRT code defines data preparation, training, evaluation, and experiment tracking.
- A SkyPilot YAML defines compute requirements, environment setup, file mounts, and the command to run.
- `q.ray` can distribute work after the requested compute is available; it does not provision that compute.

This keeps a training entry point runnable with the same `uv run ...` command on a laptop, an existing Ray cluster, or a SkyPilot-managed machine.

## Guides

- [Launch a training run](training.qmd): submit a repeatable model-training command as a managed job.
- [Develop with VS Code over SSH](vscode.qmd): launch an interactive machine and open the synchronized QRT checkout remotely.
- [Build a local Strix Halo cluster](strix-halo.qmd): schedule QRT workloads across a four-node AMD SSH pool.

## Install the CLI

Install SkyPilot as a standalone tool so it does not become a QRT project dependency. Include the extras for the infrastructure and storage backends you use; this example enables AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, RunPod, and Hugging Face Storage:

```bash
uv tool install --with pip "skypilot[aws,gcp,huggingface,kubernetes,runpod]"
sky check
```

Follow the [SkyPilot installation guide](https://docs.skypilot.ai/en/latest/getting-started/installation.html) for provider-specific credentials and extras.

Authenticate to Hugging Face interactively with `hf auth login`, or export `HF_TOKEN` and pass it to each job with `--secret HF_TOKEN`. Run `sky check huggingface` to verify the storage integration.

To connect to a team-managed SkyPilot API server instead, install the client required by the team and run `sky api login`.
